records.found: On 2026-11-03 Circulation published a peer-reviewed follow-up of vutrisiran in HELIOS-B: through 48 months, the group on the drug throughout had 37 per cent lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.63) against the group that started it later. On 2026-11-05 Intellia said its gene-editing treatment (nex-z) had advanced enrolment in its heart trial and was giving doctors a gene test for the liver-injury risk; this bears on competition and on safety.

findings.what: Circulation: HELIOS-B open-label extension, 466 people; continuous vutrisiran vs placebo-then-vutrisiran: death or cardiovascular event HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.79), death HR 0.63 (0.46 to 0.84), to month 48. Not a placebo comparison after month 36, so it adds follow-up, not a new rung.

Intellia third-quarter release: nex-z trial in the heart disease (MAGNITUDE) 'advancing enrollment'; the nerve disease trial (MAGNITUDE-2) fully enrolled, over 60; gene test results being given to investigators. The earlier liver-injury safety story is background, not restated.
Alnylam announced it would present five-year HELIOS-B data at the American Heart Association meeting; the data release itself is dated 2026-11-09, outside the window.
Clinical Research in Cardiology: early real-world use of acoramidis in Germany (StarTTR); describes use, no uptake share.

records.found: Two peer-reviewed mouse papers on partial resetting appeared. Aging Cell (2026-11-01): cyclic Yamanaka-gene switching in aged mice gave smaller stroke damage and better movement scores than normal controls. Aging (2026-10-27): a reanalysis of gene readings after seven months of resetting in aged mice found calmer inflammation in liver and kidney but signs of growth stress in the spleen. Neither is a clock-of-age result in a person, and the animal rung is already reached.

findings.what: Aging Cell: partial reprogramming (OSKM, Tet-ON mice) in aged mice reduced ischaemic brain damage vs wild-type controls; better neurological scores, preserved myelin and neurons.

Aging (Albany NY): re-analysis of RNA-seq from liver, kidney, spleen of aged mice after 7 months of partial reprogramming; benefits in liver and kidney, flagged possible genomic and proliferative stress in spleen; authors call for larger controlled studies.
Life Biosciences' latest news item is the interim data release, before the window.
